title: Topological Foundations of Multi-Field Instabilities in Continua: Part 1: Foundations Part 2:Analytical Formulation for 1-D Spin Chains Part 3: Numerical Upscaling
authors: Klaus Regenauer-Lieb, Francois Nicot, Amir Saker
abstract: This three-part series establishes a parameter-free, topological classification of multi-field instability in granular continua, extending Maxwell's rigidity count to dynamic, non-equilibrium processes.   Part 1 (Foundations): a discrete Volumetric-Mechanical-Configurational (VMC) contact formulation maps contact-scale topology to macroscopic multiphysics coupling. A Parity Theorem, $\det(\mathsf{L})=(-1)^N\det(\mathsf{L})$, forces a structural null-mode for every odd channel count $N$, creating "Gateway" layers of broken time-reversal symmetry; once the basis-invariant Gateway number $\mathcal{G}_{\rm inv}\geq 1$, gyroscopic pumping drives non-modal transient amplification along the null direction.   Part 2 (analytical, 1-D spin chains): the minimal Gateway is the $N=3$ VMC contact, whose skew block $\mathsf{L}\in\mathfrak{so}(3)$ carries a persistent zero eigenvalue and an unresisted configurational drift that operates even without friction. In an acyclic chain (first Betti number $β_1=0$) this isolates dilatancy; closed-form solutions give secular drift for $N=3$ and harmonic confinement for $N=4$.   Part 3 (numerical upscaling): quad-precision integration of tridiagonal skew-symmetric Onsager chains ($N=3$ to $50$) confirms the contrast between odd-$N$ secular drift and even-$N$ confinement on invariant tori, with even-chain frequencies scaling as $|λ_{\min}^{\rm even}|\simγπ/N$. VMC channels map to measurable DEM observables, enabling parameter-free evaluation of $\mathcal{G}$ and four falsifiable oedometer protocols.
summary: This work develops a topological theory to classify instabilities in granular materials by analyzing the structure of their multi-field coupling operators. It shows that the parity of coupled channels dictates whether the system possesses a structural null-mode, which can drive instability (the Gateway mechanism) even when classical failure indicators are not yet triggered.
main_problem: The work establishes a parameter-free, topological classification for multi-field instabilities in granular continua, extending static rigidity concepts to dynamic, non-equilibrium processes.
main_result: Instability can be predicted by the 'Gateway' mechanism—a structural null-mode appearing when the number of coupled channels ($N$) is odd—which drives transient amplification before classical failure criteria are met.
method: The analysis uses an augmented Onsager framework ($\mathbf{A} = \mathbf{D} + \mathbf{L}$), decomposing the constitutive operator into symmetric (dissipative) and skew-symmetric (conservative) parts, analyzed via spectral theory.
model_or_system: The system models granular continua using a discrete Volumetric–Mechanical–Configurational (VMC) contact formulation. The dynamics are governed by an augmented Onsager equation structure, which is then tested against linear Newton chain models and non-linear lattice extensions.
key_observables: Gateway number ($\mathcal{G}_{m inv}$), zero eigenvalues of the skew-symmetric block $\mathbf{L}$, secular drift rates, and confinement frequencies scaling with $N$.
important_parameters: The parity ($N$) of the thermodynamic channel count; the stiffness parameter ($k$); the non-linearity exponent ($n \geq 3$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on linearizing around local tangent states, though it extends to non-linear metrics by preserving the skew-symmetry of $\mathbf{L}(q)$.
figures_summary: Figures compare spectral topology for even vs. odd $N$ channels; simulations show convergence from finite stiffness (Newton) dynamics to the zero-eigenvalue Onsager limit.
paper_structure: The paper is structured in three parts: Part 1 establishes the topological foundations using VMC contacts and the Parity Theorem; Part 2 analyzes the minimal case ($N=3$) for 1D spin chains; and Part 3 numerically upscales these findings to larger systems, confirming odd-$N$ drift vs. even-$N$ confinement.
why_interesting: The topological classification of instability mechanisms in passive matter provides a powerful analogy framework that could inform the understanding of non-equilibrium dynamics or dissipation thresholds in complex quantum many-body systems where symmetry breaking is key.
